This notebook will import the source data into R, ensure the data is correctly structured and use the NHS ODS API to get the relevant organisational information

## Import Data

```{r echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=T, message=F, warning=F)
require(readr) # Tidyverse functions to read in a dataset
require(forcats) # Tidyverse functions to handle factors
require(dplyr) # Tidyverse functions to manipulate datasets
require(here) # R functions to handle file paths better

# If NHSRtools is not installed, install it
if(!require("NHSRtools")){
  devtools::install_github(("nhs-r-community/NHSRtools"))
} 
require(NHSRtools)

cdkData <- read_csv(here("data/cdk46_op_hosp.csv"))

# vmp_name, ods_code, vmp_code,  uom_name, ddd_unit, would be better handled as factors

cdkData |> 
  mutate(
    across(                   # For each column that applies below
      contains(c("_code", "_name", "_unit")),   # Columns containing "_code", "_name" or "_unit" in the name
      ~ as_factor(
          as.character(.x)    # Convert numeric values to text before converting to factor
        )
      )
    ) -> cdkData_clean        # Store as a new object

head(cdkData_clean)           # Display the first few lines of data for inspection
  
```

## Look up ODS codes for organisations

```{r echo=TRUE}
orgList <- levels(cdkData_clean$ods_code)

# Get the NHS Trust code from the ODS API
ods_get_roles() |>
  filter(display_name=="NHS TRUST") -> ODS_roles

# Lookup all NHS Trusts on the ODS API
ods_get_organisations(primary_role_id = ODS_roles$id) -> NHS_orgs

head(NHS_orgs)
```

## Join the organisation names

```{r echo=TRUE}
# 
# NHS_orgs |>
#   select(trust_name = name, ods_code = org_id)-> trimmed_NHS_orgs
# 
# 
# cdkData_clean |>
#   left_join(trimmed_NHS_orgs) -> cdkData_clean  # join the data, and save to the same object
```

## Get ICBs

```{r echo=TRUE}

ods_get_roles() |>
  filter(display_name=="INTEGRATED CARE BOARD") -> ICB_roles

ods_get_organisations( non_primary_role_id = ICB_roles$id) -> ICBs_orgs

head(ICBs_orgs)
```

## Get the trusts within the ICBs

```{r echo=TRUE}
source(here::here("r/functions/ODS_API.R"))

for (ods_code in unique(cdkData_clean$ods_code) ) {
  if(exists("ICB_trust_list")) {
    ICB_trust_list |>
    bind_rows(c(ods_code = ods_code, icb_code = ods_get_org_icb(ods_code))) ->ICB_trust_list 
  } else {
    ICB_trust_list <- 
    bind_rows(ods_code = ods_code, icb_code = ods_get_org_icb(ods_code))
  }
}

ICB_trust_list |>
  left_join(ICBs_orgs, by = c("icb_code" = "org_id")) -> ICB_trust_list

head(ICB_trust_list)
```

## Get NHS Regions

```{r echo=TRUE}


ods_get_organisations( primary_role_id = "RO209", status = "active") -> Regions

head(Regions)
```

## Get ICBs by Region

```{r}
for (Region in Regions$org_id) {
    # set the ICB name
    Region_name = min(Regions$name[Regions$org_id == Region])
    
    # call the region to ICB relationship function
    ods_get_icb_by_region(Region) |>
    mutate(Region = Region,   # Add an Region Column to the data
           Region_name = Region_name # Add an Region Name Column to the data (use first if multi)
           ) -> Region_ICB 
    
    # if Region_ICB list exists, add to it
    if(exists("Region_ICB_list")) {
      Region_ICB_list |>
        rows_append(Region_ICB) -> Region_ICB_list
    } else {
        #else - create the list
          Region_ICB_list <- Region_ICB
    }

}

head(Region_ICB_list)


```


## Get the Cancer Alliances

```{r echo=TRUE}

# Get the Cancer Network Role code from the ODS API
ods_get_roles() |>
  filter(display_name=="CANCER NETWORK") -> ODS_roles

# Lookup all NHS Trusts on the ODS API
ods_get_organisations(primary_role_id = ODS_roles$id) |>
  select(Cancer_Alliance = name,
         Alliance = org_id) -> Network_orgs

head(Network_orgs)
```

## Link Alliances to ICBs

There is no official ICB to Cancer Alliance relationship defined in the ODS data. The relationship is by region; regions can have multiple alliances. However, the [Cancer Alliance Map](https://www.england.nhs.uk/cancer/cancer-alliances-improving-care-locally/) very closely aligns with groups of ICB boundaries. As such we can manually code an ICB -\> Cancer Alliance relationship. This has been done in the CSV file data/CancerAlliances.csv.

```{r}
allianceData <- read_csv(here("data/CancerAlliances.csv"))

allianceData |>
  mutate(across(everything(),  # upper case them all
                toupper)) |>
  mutate(ICB = paste("NHS", ICS, "INTEGRATED CARE BOARD"),
         Region = paste(Region, "COMMISSIONING REGION")) |>  # expand names
  select(-ICS) |>
  left_join(Network_orgs) -> Network_orgs  # Join with the Network ODS codes

Network_orgs |>
  left_join(ICBs_orgs, by = c("ICB" = "name")) |>
  select(Cancer_Alliance, Alliance_id = Alliance, ICB, ICB_id = org_id ) -> Network_orgs


```


## Join the Trust, ICBs, Networks and regions

```{r}

Region_ICB_list |>
  select(
    ICB=org_id,    # Trim the region list to only have the info we need
    Region, 
    Region_name) -> Region_ICB_list 

ICB_trust_list |>
  rename (ICB= icb_code) |>
  left_join(Region_ICB_list) |>
  rename (ICB_id = ICB) |>
  left_join(Network_orgs, by = "ICB_id")-> ICB_trust_list

head(ICB_trust_list)
```

##  Check for superceeded organisations

Organisations which have been renamed etc will not map to their current ICB automatically.   There is a predecessor / successor function in the ODS which we can use to map them.

```{r}
# Find any organisation id in the drug data which is missing in the ICB_trust_list
ods_list <- unique(cdkData_clean$ods_code)

active_ods_list <- unique(ICB_trust_list$ods_code[!is.na(ICB_trust_list$ICB_id)])

old_orgs <- ods_list[!ods_list %in% active_ods_list]

for(org in old_orgs) {
  if(exists("successor")) {
    successor |> 
    bind_rows(c(new_code = ods_get_org_successor(org), ods_code = org)) -> successor
  } else {
    bind_rows(c(new_code = ods_get_org_successor(org), ods_code = org)) -> successor
  }
}

cdkData_clean |>
  left_join(successor) |>
  mutate(new_code = case_when(
    is.na(new_code) ~ ods_code, 
            T ~ new_code)
  ) -> cdkData_clean_with_successors
```
## Join the Trusts, ICBs and Alliances to Drug Data

```{r}
ICB_trust_list |>
  select(ods_code, ICB_id, ICB_name = name, Region_id = Region, Region_name, Alliance_id, Alliance_name = Cancer_Alliance) -> ICB_trust_list

cdkData_clean_with_successors |>
  left_join(ICB_trust_list, by=c("new_code" ="ods_code" )) -> cdkData_clean_with_structure

NHS_orgs |>
  select(Trust_name = name, org_id) -> NHS_orgs

cdkData_clean_with_structure |>
  left_join(NHS_orgs, by =c("new_code" ="org_id" ) ) -> cdkData_clean_with_structure

cdkData_clean_with_structure |>
  mutate(
    across(                   # For each column that applies below
      contains(c("_code", "_name", "_unit", "uom", "_id")),   # Columns containing "_code",
                                                              #"_name" or "_unit" in the name
      ~ as_factor(
          as.character(.x)    # Convert numeric values to text before converting to factor
        )
      )
    ) -> cdkData_clean_with_structure        # Store 

  
  
cdkData_clean_with_structure

saveRDS(cdkData_clean_with_structure, here::here("data/cdk46_op_hosp_clean.RDS"))
write_csv(cdkData_clean_with_structure, here::here("data/cdk46_op_hosp_clean.csv"))
```
